pdf-item-equation-1-1.Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution: `IsSmoothSolution` requires both equations in (1.1) at every positive time when the viscosity is $1$. It also requires velocity and pressure smooth up to $t=0$ and fixes the initial velocity there. The definition describes a global solution on the whole time half-line.

s1-viscosity.Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace: The passage explains how viscosity $1$ gives every $\nu>0$ by rescaling time, velocity and pressure. The definition `BreakdownOnSpace` places $\forall\,\nu>0$ directly in the target. For each viscosity it asks for smooth compactly supported solenoidal data that admit no global smooth solution with one uniform energy bound.
s1-viscosity.Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus: The viscosity rescaling preserves spatial period one because it changes the time and amplitudes only. The definition `BreakdownOnTorus` puts every $\nu>0$ in the target and asks for smooth periodic solenoidal data with no global smooth solution whose velocity has period one. Smooth pressure on $\mathbb R^3$ is allowed without a periodicity constraint.

s1-domains.Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace: `BreakdownOnSpace` defines the whole-space nonexistence target behind the regularity question. For every $\nu>0$ it asks for a smooth compactly supported divergence-free datum that admits no global smooth solution with a single bound on $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|u(t,x)|^2\,dx$ for all $t\ge0$.
s1-domains.Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus: `BreakdownOnTorus` defines the periodic nonexistence target behind the regularity question. At each positive viscosity it asks for smooth solenoidal data of period one that admit no global smooth velocity of period one. The pressure in the excluded class can be any smooth field on $\mathbb R^3$.

s1-headline.Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile: `breakdownOnSpace_of_profile` proves whole-space nonexistence at every positive viscosity from a supplied smooth, nonzero velocity profile periodic up to an isometry. It assumes spatial decay through two derivatives of the velocity and decay of the pressure gradient. Its conclusion excludes global smooth solutions with uniformly bounded energy for some compactly supported solenoidal datum. The paper's headline also describes a finite-time trajectory, whose rate and profile error are outside this declaration's conclusion.
s1-headline.Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p: `breakdownOnTorus_of_profile` assumes a smooth, nonzero recurrent profile with decay through two spatial derivatives and decay of the pressure gradient. It proves that at each positive viscosity some smooth solenoidal periodic datum admits no global smooth solution with periodic velocity, allowing arbitrary smooth pressure. The paper's finite-time trajectory and its quantitative estimates are separate from this nonexistence conclusion.

s1-fefferman.Breakdown.BreakdownOnSpace: `BreakdownOnSpace` defines nonexistence of a global smooth solution with one uniform kinetic-energy bound, for some smooth compactly supported solenoidal datum at every $\nu>0$. Separate theorems derive it from a profile or certificate hypothesis. The definition gives no finite blow-up time, rate or profile estimate. `BreakdownOnSpace` uses smooth compactly supported data and excludes global smooth solutions with uniformly bounded energy, a precise special choice of the rapidly decaying data in the cited formulation.
s1-fefferman.Breakdown.BreakdownOnTorus: `BreakdownOnTorus` defines a target: for every $\nu>0$ some smooth period-one divergence-free datum admits no global smooth solution whose velocity is periodic. It allows any smooth pressure. Fefferman's appended erratum also requires the pressure to be periodic. Thus the formal exclusion covers a larger solution class than the corrected periodic formulation. The definition itself supplies no proof of that exclusion.

s1-profile-reduction.Breakdown.breakdownOnSpace_of_profile: `breakdownOnSpace_of_profile` is the whole-space implication in the announced reduction. Its premise supplies a nonzero smooth profile solving the similarity equations, with positive period up to an isometry, velocity decay through two spatial derivatives and pressure-gradient decay. From it Lean derives nonexistence of a global smooth solution with a uniform energy bound for suitable compactly supported solenoidal data at every $\nu>0$.
s1-profile-reduction.Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p: `breakdownOnTorus_of_profile` is the periodic implication in the announced reduction. It takes a nonzero smooth profile solving the similarity equations, with positive period up to an isometry, velocity decay through two spatial derivatives and pressure-gradient decay. It gives periodic solenoidal data that exclude global smooth periodic velocity for every $\nu>0$, even with smooth pressure allowed to be nonperiodic.

s1-finite-codimension-summary.Breakdown.DichotomyHolds: For $T=T_0+C$ on a real Hilbert space with $C$ compact and $\|T_0\|\le b\le\alpha<\beta$, there are $\alpha<r_1<r_2<\beta$, $K>0$ and a finite-rank projection $P_u$ commuting with $T$ with $\|T^n(I-P_u)\|\le Kr_1^n$ and $\|P_ux\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|T^nP_ux\|$. `DichotomyHolds` provides a finite-dimensional commuting projection for every compact perturbation of a small bounded operator, without assuming a particular unstable eigenvalue. It is the spectral input rather than the nonlinear stability conclusion.
s1-finite-codimension-summary.Breakdown.StepDataStatement: For a recurrent profile and any dense $C'$ and $t_0>0$, asserts $k\ge1$, $\theta$ with $e^{-S/(4k)}<\theta<1$, $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, a finite-dimensional $V$, $J$ into $C'$ and a bounded $\mathcal R$ solving the linear correction on successive intervals. Proposition 4.3 uses a global weighted curve. The correction component of the linear right inverse lies in a fixed finite-dimensional space. Nonlinear stability and the physical norm identification require the subsequent contraction and realization.

s1-certificate-summary.Breakdown.certificate_orbit: `certificate_orbit` takes a supplied `CertificateHypothesis` and produces a nonzero weak recurrent profile. This declaration uses the earlier rectangular parameter family and its analytic and smallness assumptions. The passage refers to the later 7.3 certificate with its own quantitative conclusions and subsequent smoothing. The input certificate and its numerical verification are separate from this implication.

s1-profile-domain.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: `PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` quantifies over a positive period and a linear isometry of $\mathbb R^3$. The recurrence has the form $W(s+S,y)=R W(s,R^{-1}y)$, so the isometry acts on both the argument and the vector. The definition also requires a smooth nonzero solution and decay of the velocity and pressure gradient.

s1-profile-smoothness.Breakdown.PeriodicSimilarityProfileExist: `PeriodicSimilarityProfileExists` asks for jointly smooth velocity and pressure and requires the similarity equation, zero divergence and nonzero recurrent velocity. It includes uniform decay through two spatial derivatives of $W$ and the first derivative of $q$. An existence proof has to supply a profile satisfying this definition.

This is the algebraic component of the method described here.

s1-stable-convergence.Breakdown.TransferHolds: For the continuous mild curve $u:[0,1)\to X$ and recurrent orbit $w:\mathbb R\to X$ supplied by the formal transfer assertion, there are $A\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa>0$ with $\|D_{1-t}u(t)-w(-\log(1-t))\|_X\le A(1-t)^\kappa$. Writing $s=-\log(1-t)$ gives $Ae^{-\kappa s}\to0$. In the Navier–Stokes application $X=\dot H^1_{\rm div}(\mathbb R^3)$ and $D_\mu f(x)=\sqrt\mu f(\sqrt\mu x)$. This compares the convergence conclusion alone, and asserts no nonuniqueness result.

s1-unforced.Breakdown.IsSmoothSolution:
The field `momentum` in `IsSmoothSolution` requires $\partial_tu+(u\cdot
abla)u=
u\Delta u-
abla p$ at positive times. It has the same zero forcing as the paper's equation.

s1-outline-base-solution.Breakdown.Periodic.selfSimilarSolves: For a smooth profile with the decay bounds and $T>0$, $u(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1/2}W(s,y)$ and $p=(T-t)^{-1}q(s,y)$, centred at $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$, are smooth on $(-\infty,T)\times\mathbb R^3$ and solve Navier–Stokes there. Recurrence is not needed. No extension through $T$. `selfSimilarSolves` supplies the classical unforced solution for a translated centre and the stronger smooth-profile premise. The perturbative construction is a further theorem.
s1-outline-base-solution.Breakdown.TransferHolds: `TransferHolds` starts with a recurrent mild orbit and constructs a nearby mild curve whose difference from the orbit decays after dilation. This is the perturbation part of the passage. Identifying the recurrent orbit with the physical solution (1.4) and recovering smooth velocity and pressure require realization results.

s1-outline-contraction.Breakdown.ContractionStatement: Given a bounded linear $R$ solving the linear recurrence $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$, $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$, each small $\xi$ yields $e$ with $\|e\|\le C_1\|\xi\|$ and bounded $z$ solving the quadratic version with $\theta^nN(z_n,z_n)$. This is the discrete step only. The application takes $Y=C([0,h];X)$, but this formal statement allows any real Banach space $Y$. The correspondence between the sequence solution and the continuous physical mild equation is an additional step.

s1-outline-space.Breakdown.Freq.X: Here $X$ is the real Hilbert subspace of $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ consisting of $g(-\xi)=\overline{g(\xi)}$ and $\xi\cdot g(\xi)=0$ almost everywhere. A physical velocity is represented by $g=2\pi|\xi|\widehat u$, and the reconstructed velocity belongs to $L^6$. The norm corresponds to $\|\nabla u\|_2$. The definition is made in frequency space, whereas the paper defines $X$ by physical $L^6$ fields with weak gradient in $L^2$. Reconstruction and the norm-identification theorems are needed to identify these descriptions. This definition alone does not prove a uniform bound for the profile slices or a physical-space completion theorem.
s1-outline-space.Breakdown.Freq.gradSixDecay: For every smooth divergence-free $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying $|f(y)|\le A/(1+|y|)$ and $\|Df(y)\|_{\rm op}\le A/(1+|y|)^2$ for some finite $A$, one universal constant $C$ gives $f\in L^6$ and $\|f\|_6\le C(\int\sum_i|\partial_i f|^2)^{1/2}$. Applied to $W(s)$, the decay assumptions make the right-hand side uniformly finite. The formal statement is restricted to this smooth decay class and does not define all of $\dot H^1_{\rm div}$.

s1-outline-torus-space.Breakdown.Periodic.V: The period-one space of sequences $a(n)\in\mathbb C^3$, square summable, with $a(-n)=\overline{a(n)}$ and $n\cdot a(n)=0$, with inhomogeneous $H^1$ norm. Nonzero constants are included. (3.15) instead uses the homogeneous norm on mean-zero fields of any period. The formal unit-torus space uses the inhomogeneous $H^1$ weight $1+4\pi^2|k|^2$ and retains the zero Fourier coefficient. Mean zero is not part of that space definition.

s1-outline-regularity.Breakdown.MildRegular: `MildRegular` states the regularity property for a whole-space mild curve on a closed interval starting from a smooth compactly supported solenoidal datum. It supplies smooth velocity and pressure, the Navier–Stokes equation at interior times and uniform bounds on energy, velocity and its spatial derivative. It identifies the smooth velocity with the mild curve almost everywhere in space at each time. Periodic regularity is a separate result.

s1-outline-similarity-equation.Breakdown.SimilarityResidual:
`SimilarityResidual` defines the vector expression $\partial_sW+ rac12W+ rac12(y\cdot
abla)W-\Delta W+(W\cdot
abla)W+
abla q$. It does not assert that it vanishes, that $W$ is divergence-free or recurrent, or that $W$ is differentiable. The formal expression records the similarity momentum equation, but the definition alone does not prove equivalence under the change of variables.
s1-outline-similarity-equation.Breakdown.physicalField: `physicalField` defines $u(t,x)=(1-t)^{-1/2}W(s_0-\log(1-t),x/\sqrt{1-t})$, agreeing with (1.4) for $T=1$, $s_0=0$. It has no hypotheses. By the conventions it is zero for $t\ge1$, with no solution claim there. `physicalField` supplies the final-time-one transformation. Classical differentiability and the equations are required for the equivalence.

s1-outline-target.Breakdown.MildFramework.IsOrbit: `IsOrbit` defines a recurrent mild profile: continuous $w$, nonzero at some time, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$ for a surjective isometry $\rho$ and $S>0$, satisfying the similarity-time mild equation for all $s'\le s$, under the heat, bilinear, dilation and compactness assumptions. No pressure or decay. The formal orbit condition combines the similarity mild equation with recurrence under an isometry.
s1-outline-target.Breakdown.TransferHolds: `TransferHolds` defines the property that for every dense subspace $C$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is a mild solution $u$ on $[0,1)$ with $u(0)\in C$, $\|u(0)-w(0)\|<\varepsilon$ and $\|D_{1-t}u(t)-w(-\log(1-t))\|\le A(1-t)^\kappa$. It does not require $\kappa<1/4$ or state the two-sided rate. The formal transfer assertion obtains convergence in the Hilbert norm with an explicit exponentially decaying bound $Ce^{-\kappa s}$ for some $\kappa>0$.

s1-outline-subcritical.Breakdown.dilateField: `dilateField` defines $D_\mu u(x)=\sqrt\mu\,u(\sqrt\mu x)$, the paper's Navier–Stokes dilation for $\mu>0$. For $\mu\le0$ the square root is taken as zero, giving the zero field. The identities in (3.5) use only $\mu>0$.

u}=D_\mu D_
u$ and $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$. These are the three identities of (3.5) in the Fourier representation. The formal norm law is exactly the factor $\mu^{1/4}$ for positive dilation parameters.

s1-outline-free-flow.Breakdown.Freq.heat_holds: On $X$, $G(0)=I$, $G(s+t)=G(s)G(t)$ and $\|G(t)\|\le1$ for $s,t\ge0$, $t\mapsto G(t)g$ is continuous on $[0,\infty)$, and $G(t)$ is self-adjoint for all real $t$. u}=D_\mu D_
u$ and $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$. These are the three identities of (3.5) in the Fourier representation. The dilation factor at $\mu=e^{-s}$ is $e^{-s/4}$. Applying the heat contraction gives the stated bound for $s\ge0$.

s1-outline-monodromy.Breakdown.MonodromyStatement: For a recurrent profile with $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, each $I-A_n$ is invertible with inverse norm at most $4/3$, $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $M-\rho^{-1}(D_\mu G(L))^k$ is compact, and $\|\rho^{-1}(D_\mu G(L))^k\|\le e^{-S/4}$, as in Lemma 4.4 for the split product. s1-outline-compactness.Breakdown.monodromy: For a supplied $k\ge1$ with $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, each $I-A_n$ has inverse norm at most $4/3$, $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, and the period map $\mathcal M$ differs by a compact operator from the free map $\mathcal M_0$, with $\|\mathcal M_0\|\le e^{-S/4}$. s1-outline-spectrum.Breakdown.MonodromyStatement: For a recurrent profile with $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, each $I-A_n$ is invertible with inverse norm at most $4/3$, $S_{n+k}=\rho S_n\rho^{-1}$, $M-\rho^{-1}(D_\mu G(L))^k$ is compact, and $\|\rho^{-1}(D_\mu G(L))^k\|\le e^{-S/4}$, as in Lemma 4.4 for the split product. s1-outline-spectrum.Breakdown.DichotomyHolds: For $T=T_0+C$ on a real Hilbert space with $C$ compact and $\|T_0\|\le b\le\alpha<\beta$, there are $\alpha<r_1<r_2<\beta$, $K>0$ and a finite-rank projection $P_u$ commuting with $T$ with $\|T^n(I-P_u)\|\le Kr_1^n$ and $\|P_ux\|\le Kr_2^{-n}\|T^nP_ux\|$. s1-outline-finite-corrections.Breakdown.StepDataStatement: For a recurrent profile and any dense $C'$ and $t_0>0$, asserts $k\ge1$, $\theta$ with $e^{-S/(4k)}<\theta<1$, $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, a finite-dimensional $V$, $J$ into $C'$ and a bounded $\mathcal R$ solving the linear correction on successive intervals. s1-outline-right-inverse.Breakdown.StepDataStatement: For a recurrent profile and any dense $C'$ and $t_0>0$, asserts $k\ge1$, $\theta$ with $e^{-S/(4k)}<\theta<1$, $\|A_n\|\le1/4$, a finite-dimensional $V$, $J$ into $C'$ and a bounded $\mathcal R$ solving the linear correction on successive intervals. s1-outline-dense-data.Breakdown.Freq.testDense_holds: The span of $J\varphi=2\pi|\xi|\hat\varphi$ over smooth compactly supported divergence-free $\varphi$ is dense in $X$, and also dense in the graph norm of $-\Delta$. The first gives the density used in 3.1. The second is additional. `testDense_holds` supplies density of embedded smooth compactly supported divergence-free fields and additionally density in the graph norm of the Laplacian.
s1-outline-dense-data.Breakdown.Freq.testSpan_holds: Every element of the real span of the classes $J\varphi$, over smooth compactly supported divergence-free $\varphi$, equals $J\varphi$ for a single such field. It does not state density of the span in $X$. `testSpan_holds` identifies every element of the linear span of represented test fields with one smooth compactly supported divergence-free field. It does not itself assert that this span is dense.
s1-outline-dense-data.Breakdown.SectionStatement: For a bounded finite-rank projection $P$ and a dense subspace $C'$ of a real Banach space, asserts a bounded linear $J$ with $PJ=P$ and range in $C'$. It does not bound $\|J\|$ or say the full image of $J$ is finite-dimensional. A finite-rank projection and a dense linear subspace admit a bounded map $J$ preserving the projected component and taking values in the dense subspace. Its restriction to the finite-dimensional range supplies the smooth correction space.

s1-outline-contraction-nearby.Breakdown.ContractionStatement: Given a bounded linear $R$ solving the linear recurrence $z_0-A_0z_0-\Gamma Je=g_0$, $z_n-A_nz_n-\theta^{-1}\Gamma Ez_{n-1}=g_n$, each small $\xi$ yields $e$ with $\|e\|\le C_1\|\xi\|$ and bounded $z$ solving the quadratic version with $\theta^nN(z_n,z_n)$. The finite-dimensional correction space and the identification with a continuous-time mild solution come from separate ingredients.
s1-outline-contraction-nearby.Breakdown.TransferHolds: `TransferHolds` defines the property that for every dense subspace $C$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is a mild solution $u$ on $[0,1)$ with $u(0)\in C$, $\|u(0)-w(0)\|<\varepsilon$ and $\|D_{1-t}u(t)-w(-\log(1-t))\|\le A(1-t)^\kappa$. It does not require $\kappa<1/4$ or state the two-sided rate. The paper's statement starts with each nearby prescribed datum and corrects it in a fixed finite-dimensional space. That stronger quantifier is not retained here.

s1-outline-fixed-time.Breakdown.TransferHolds: `TransferHolds` defines the property that for every dense subspace $C$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is a mild solution $u$ on $[0,1)$ with $u(0)\in C$, $\|u(0)-w(0)\|<\varepsilon$ and $\|D_{1-t}u(t)-w(-\log(1-t))\|\le A(1-t)^\kappa$. It does not require $\kappa<1/4$ or state the two-sided rate. The formal error compares the constructed curve with the fixed orbit at phase $-\log(1-t)$ and final time one. No time, spatial or phase-modulation parameter occurs in that conclusion.

s1-outline-vector-potential.Breakdown.Periodic.homotopyPotential: `homotopyPotential` integrates $s\,g(x_0+s(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)$ for $0\le s\le1$. Set $x_0=0$ and $g=u^*(t)$ to get the paper's $A(t)$. The curl identity $\operatorname{curl}A=g$ uses smoothness and zero divergence of $g$ and is proved separately.
s1-outline-vector-potential.Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffField: `cutoffField` defines $\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A$. When $\operatorname{curl}A=g$, the product rule identifies this expression with the paper's $\operatorname{curl}(\chi A)$. Its application takes $g=u^*(t)$, a potential centred at the origin, and $\chi(x)=\eta(x/r)$.
s1-outline-vector-potential.Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffDivergenceFree: Multiplying $g$ by $\chi$ creates the divergence term $\nabla\chi\cdot g$. Given `HomotopyCurl`, the identity $\operatorname{curl}A=g$ makes the correction $\nabla\chi\times A$ cancel that term. `cutoffDivergenceFree` proves the resulting field smooth and divergence-free for smooth $\chi$ and smooth solenoidal $g$. The proof also uses symmetry of second derivatives of $\chi$.

s1-outline-cutoff-error.Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties: `approxFieldProperties_holds` uses profile decay and a smooth cutoff about the centre of a unit periodic cell. It gives exact agreement within radius $1/16$ and exact vanishing at and beyond radius $1/8$, as well as smoothness and zero divergence. The gradient-error estimate in the passage is a separate declaration.
s1-outline-cutoff-error.Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffGradientClose: `cutoffGradientClose` assumes `ApproxFieldProperties` and a smooth decaying similarity profile. It makes the cutoff's squared gradient error as small as desired in similarity coordinates by taking $T-t$ small, so the fixed physical cutoff radius becomes large in those coordinates. The paper gives a power-law estimate for every physical radius $r$.

s1-outline-datum-only.Breakdown.TransferHolds: `TransferHolds` allows the initial datum to be chosen from a dense subspace, such as the smooth compactly supported solenoidal fields. The mild solution then tracks the uncut recurrent orbit. The paper obtains a candidate explicitly by cutting off the initial trace and adding a correction. The abstract statement quantifies over the subspace and a tolerance, leaving the actual choice of datum existential.
s1-outline-datum-only.Breakdown.Periodic.cutoffField: `cutoffField` defines $\bar g=\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A_{x_0,g}$ with $A_{x_0,g}(x)=\int_0^1\sigma g(x_0+\sigma(x-x_0))\times(x-x_0)\,d\sigma$, the expanded formula in the proof of Lemma 5.1. It assumes no smoothness and asserts neither smoothness nor support. The formal expression supplies the cutoff construction. It does not select the large radius or prove the resulting blow-up solution.

s1-outline-torus-scaling.Breakdown.Periodic.selfSimilarSolves: `selfSimilarSolves` concerns a whole-space field, centred at $a=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$: for $T>0$, $u(t,x)=(T-t)^{-1/2}W(\log(T/(T-t)),(x-a)/\sqrt{T-t})$ and the corresponding pressure solve the viscosity-one equations for all $t<T$, assuming a smooth similarity profile with the formal decay bounds. This field is not asserted to be spatially periodic. It is used later in the unit-cell construction. It does not state the paper's transformation from a torus of side $L$ to one of side one.
s1-outline-torus-scaling.Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup: `TorusBlowup` defines the assertion that some smooth period-one divergence-free $u_0$, some $T>0$ and a continuous mild curve on $[0,T)$ from $u_0$ have $\sup_{0\le t<T}\|u(t)\|=\infty$ in inhomogeneous $H^1$. It imposes neither $T\le1$ nor (2.6), and gives no rate. The final formal condition records some positive time and an unbounded periodic mild trajectory, without the identity $T=L^{-2}$.

s1-outline-torus-approximation.Breakdown.Periodic.approxFieldProperties: For a profile with the decay bounds and every $T>0$, the cutoff $\bar u=\chi g+\nabla\chi\times A_g$ is smooth on $(-\infty,T)\times\mathbb R^3$, divergence-free, zero for $|x-a|\ge1/8$ and equal to $g$ for $|x-a|\le1/16$; $\bar p$ is smooth with the same support. No norm estimate is given. The formal cutoff is centred at $(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ on a unit cell, equals the translated profile inside radius $1/16$, and vanishes outside radius $1/8$. The paper first uses radii proportional to $L$.

s1-outline-kernel-decay.Breakdown.FarField.lerayKernelBound_hold: One constant $C$ gives $|H_{ijk}(\tau,x)|\le C/(|x|+\sqrt\tau)^4$ for all $i,j,k$, $\tau>0$ and $x$. The paper's (3.9) covers every derivative order $l$. This is its first-derivative case only. The formal kernel estimate is $C(|x|+\sqrt\tau)^{-4}$ for all $\tau>0$ and all $x$, which implies the stated time-uniform $C|x|^{-4}$ estimate away from the origin.

s1-outline-flow-comparison.Breakdown.Periodic.FreeHeatComparison: `FreeHeatComparison` defines local convergence of the rescaled periodic free heat flow for each compact smooth solenoidal datum, uniformly on a compact forward time interval. It gives no explicit power of the period, unlike the bound $CL^{-5/2}\|f\|_1$ in (6.3). `FreeHeatComparison` is local convergence of the rescaled free heat flow in a product of gradient $L^2$ and velocity $L^6$ norms, with an arbitrary tolerance. It gives no explicit global $L^{-1/2}$ rate.
s1-outline-flow-comparison.Breakdown.Periodic.HeatDivFreeComparison: `HeatDivFreeComparison` defines a local comparison: for small $\mu$ and $\tau\in[\varepsilon,\varepsilon^{-1}]$, the rescaled periodic projected heat flow of a transplanted $A\in L^2$ supported in $\overline B_{b'}$ is within $\delta\|A\|_{3/2}$ of $e^{\tau\Delta}\mathbb PA$ on $B_b$. Paper (6.2) has $CL^{-7/2}\|F\|_1$. `HeatDivFreeComparison` is a local operator comparison for compactly supported $L^2$ right-hand sides on heat times bounded away from zero. It gives no explicit global $L^{-5/2}$ rate.

s1-outline-neumann.Breakdown.Periodic.rightInversePerturb: Let $E,F$ be real Banach spaces, let $A,A_1:E\to F$ and $R:F\to E$ be bounded linear, and suppose $AR=I_F$, $\|R\|\le K$ and $\|A_1-A\|K\le1/2$. The formal theorem supplies $R_1:F\to E$ with $A_1R_1=I_F$ and $\|R_1\|\le2K$. The proof corrects the defect by the inverse of $I_F+(A_1-A)R$. In 6 the heat-flow comparison is used to verify the smallness assumption. This abstract theorem alone gives no lower threshold for $L$.

s1-outline-torus-final.Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation: `SeqPerturbation` supplies exact mild pieces that match at the endpoints once the normalized residuals are small and the linear sequence problem has a bounded right inverse. s1-outline-torus-final.Breakdown.Periodic.TorusBlowup: `TorusBlowup` defines the assertion that some smooth period-one divergence-free $u_0$, some $T>0$ and a continuous mild curve on $[0,T)$ from $u_0$ have $\sup_{0\le t<T}\|u(t)\|=\infty$ in inhomogeneous $H^1$. s1-outline-unforced-correction.Breakdown.Periodic.breakdownOnTorus_of_p: A smooth recurrent nonzero profile with the stated decay implies, for each $\nu>0$, a smooth period-one divergence-free $u_0$ with no global smooth periodic-velocity solution. It does not state the cutoff-error correction or identify the corrected finite-time trajectory asserted here.

s1-conventions-fourier.Breakdown.Freq.freqTrL2: The unitary Fourier transform on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ with character $e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}$. ns-3late-periodic-heat-laws.Breakdown.Periodic.heat_add: For $s,t\ge0$, composing the two Gaussian multipliers adds their time parameters. `heat_add` gives the resulting semigroup law on the unit torus.
ns-3late-periodic-heat-laws.Breakdown.Periodic.norm_heat_le: `norm_heat_le` bounds the heat operator norm by one. Each Fourier multiplier has modulus at most one for positive time. The assigned identity gives the same bound at nonpositive times in Lean’s unit-torus model.
ns-3late-periodic-heat-laws.Breakdown.Periodic.heat_continuousOn: `heat_continuousOn` proves strong continuity on $[0,\infty)$ in the inhomogeneous unit-torus norm. The paper uses strong continuity on its homogeneous mean-zero space for each period.

s3-periodic-sobolev-proof-dependency.Breakdown.Periodic.kernelSharpBound_hold: `kernelSharpBound_holds` uses a Sobolev estimate for finite Fourier sums to control the periodic trilinear pairing and then the bilinear heat kernel. Lean uses the inhomogeneous norm on the unit torus for that estimate. The Sobolev inequality cited here in the paper is for the homogeneous norm of mean-zero fields on a torus of any side length.

pdf-item-equation-3-18.Breakdown.Periodic.TrigHs: There is one $C>0$ such that every finite Fourier sum $p(x)=\sum_{n\in F}e^{2\pi i n\cdot x}c_n$, $c_n\in\mathbb C^3$, obeys $\|p\|_{L^6([0,1]^3)}\le C(\sum_{n\in F}(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c_n|^2)^{1/2}$. No reality, solenoidality or mean-zero hypothesis is imposed. Equation (3.18) instead concerns all mean-zero fields, with a homogeneous gradient norm and one constant for every period $L>0$. The linked definition states this finite-sum assertion.
pdf-item-equation-3-18.Breakdown.Periodic.trigHs: There is one $C>0$ such that every finite Fourier sum $p(x)=\sum_{n\in F}e^{2\pi i n\cdot x}c_n$, $c_n\in\mathbb C^3$, obeys $\|p\|_{L^6([0,1]^3)}\le C(\sum_{n\in F}(1+4\pi^2|n|^2)|c_n|^2)^{1/2}$. No reality, solenoidality or mean-zero hypothesis is imposed. Equation (3.18) instead concerns all mean-zero fields, with a homogeneous gradient norm and one constant for every period $L>0$. The linked theorem proves this finite-sum assertion. Extension and period scaling are additional steps.

pdf-item-theorem-3-7.Breakdown.Periodic.ShellTorus.Internal.s: Assume the inhomogeneous unit-torus $L^6$ Sobolev inequality for all finite complex vector Fourier sums. Let $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$, $\tau>0$ and $\mu\tau\le1$. For $A\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ vanishing almost everywhere outside $\overline B_b$, place $f_\mu(x)=A((x-c)/\sqrt\mu)$ in the cell about $c=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and extend it periodically. The formal theorem gives $\|e^{\mu\tau\Delta}\mathbb P f_\mu\|_{H^1(\mathbb T^3)}\le C\mu^{1/4}\tau^{-3/4}\|A\|_{3/2}$ with one $C$. Compact support makes this $L^{3/2}$ norm finite. Equation (3.19) allows all mean-zero $L^{3/2}$ forces, all periods and all positive times. It uses the homogeneous norm. This comparison covers the linear estimate. The lemma also states shift, continuity and a bilinear estimate.
pdf-item-theorem-3-7.Breakdown.Periodic.Forced.Internal.force: `forceV_eq_heat` proves the shift part of Lemma 3.7. Starting the projected heat field at an earlier positive lag and applying heat for the lag difference gives the same field as starting at the later lag. On each unit-torus Fourier coefficient this is a product of Gaussian factors.
pdf-item-theorem-3-7.Breakdown.Periodic.SourceCont.Internal.f: `forceV_continuousOn` proves the continuity part of Lemma 3.7 for the projected heat field at positive lags. The field is read in the inhomogeneous unit-torus norm. The separate norm estimates and the mean-zero property of advective forcing require other arguments.
pdf-item-theorem-3-7.Breakdown.Periodic.kernelSharpBound_hold: `kernelSharpBound_holds` proves the bilinear estimate of order $\tau^{-3/4}$ in Lemma 3.7. It applies for $0<\tau\le1$ in the inhomogeneous unit-torus norm. The paper’s bound uses homogeneous mean-zero norms at every period and is stated for all positive lags.

ns-3late-periodic-force-bound.Breakdown.Periodic.ShellTorus.Internal.s: Assume the inhomogeneous unit-torus $L^6$ Sobolev inequality for all finite complex vector Fourier sums. Let $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$, $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$, $\tau>0$ and $\mu\tau\le1$. For $A\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ vanishing almost everywhere outside $\overline B_b$, place $f_\mu(x)=A((x-c)/\sqrt\mu)$ in the cell about $c=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$ and extend it periodically. The formal theorem gives $\|e^{\mu\tau\Delta}\mathbb P f_\mu\|_{H^1(\mathbb T^3)}\le C\mu^{1/4}\tau^{-3/4}\|A\|_{3/2}$ with one $C$. Compact support makes this $L^{3/2}$ norm finite. Equation (3.19) allows all mean-zero $L^{3/2}$ forces, all periods and all positive times. It uses the homogeneous norm.

ns-3late-periodic-force-shift.Breakdown.Periodic.Forced.Internal.force: `forceV_eq_heat` supplies $F(r+t)=G(t)F(r)$ at period one for $r>0$ and $t\ge0$. The projection has already been applied in $F(r)$, so the extra heat factor advances the same coefficient by time $t$. Continuity is a separate conclusion.
ns-3late-periodic-force-shift.Breakdown.Periodic.SourceCont.Internal.f: `forceV_continuousOn` concerns the other clause of this sentence: the projected heat field varies continuously with positive lag in the inhomogeneous unit-torus norm. The equality relating two different lags is supplied by the heat-shift theorem.

ns-3late-periodic-kernel-bound.Breakdown.Periodic.KernelSharpBound: `KernelSharpBound` is the proposition asserting a uniform bound of order $\tau^{-3/4}$ for the bilinear map, in the inhomogeneous unit-torus norm and for $0<\tau\le1$. The paper’s (3.20) uses homogeneous mean-zero norms at every period and all positive lags.
ns-3late-periodic-kernel-bound.Breakdown.Periodic.kernelSharpBound_hold: `kernelSharpBound_holds` proves the short-time bilinear estimate on the unit torus. In this proof a Sobolev estimate for Fourier sums controls the trilinear pairing that bounds the bilinear operator. The paper states the resulting type of estimate in a homogeneous norm and for arbitrary period.

ns-3late-periodic-abstract-realization.Breakdown.Periodic.stepFrame: `stepFrame` packages the heat and bilinear laws used later at each time scale. Given the short-lag bilinear bound, it replaces $G(t)$ by $G(\mu t)$ and the kernel by $\mu^{3/4}K_{\mathbb T}(\mu\tau)$ for $0<\mu\le1$. The prefactor cancels the change in the short-lag constant. Lean keeps the spatial torus fixed.

pdf-item-equation-3-21.Breakdown.Periodic.TransplantNorm: For a smooth compactly supported solenoidal $g:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$, assume $\operatorname{supp}g\subseteq\overline B_b$, $0<\mu\le1$, $b>0$ and $\sqrt\mu b\le1/8$. Transplant $g$ to the unit torus as $\mu^{-1/2}g((x-c)/\sqrt\mu)$ in the cell about $c=(1/2,1/2,1/2)$, with periodic extension. The formal assertion states that the squared inhomogeneous norm after multiplying this field by $\mu^{1/4}$ equals $\|\nabla g\|_2^2+\mu\|g\|_2^2$. Equation (3.21) instead relates homogeneous norms of an arbitrary periodic field on two different tori. The same numbered equation also states heat and bilinear covariance between periods. This assertion contains neither.
pdf-item-equation-3-21.Breakdown.Periodic.stepFrame: Equation (3.21) compares a field on tori of two different periods. `stepFrame` instead keeps the unit torus fixed and rescales the heat and bilinear clocks. With the original short-lag bound, multiplication by $\mu^{3/4}$ preserves its constant after the lag is changed to $\mu\tau$.

ns-s4-001.Breakdown.stepData: `stepData` uses the spectral dichotomy to construct a bounded inverse on sequences of normalized intervals for the equation linearized about the recurrent orbit. It gives a finite-dimensional coordinate $e$ with datum adjustment $Je$ in a chosen dense subspace. Proposition 4.3 describes the corresponding inverse in one weighted space on $[0,1)$.
ns-s4-001.Breakdown.Periodic.SeqPerturbation: `SeqPerturbation` takes the bounded linear right inverse as input. If the approximate curves and the change to the initial datum have small residuals in the normalized interval norms, it asserts the existence of nonlinear corrections that match at the interval endpoints. This is the step after the linear inverse announced in this passage.

pdf-item-equation-4-1.Breakdown.physicalField: For $t<1$, set $u_{s_0}(t,x)=(1-t)^{-1/2}W(s_0-\log(1-t),x/\sqrt{1-t})$. The formal definition contains no inequality. From the order-zero profile bound $|W(s,y)|\le C/(1+|y|)$ one obtains $|u_{s_0}(t,x)|\le C/(\sqrt{1-t}+|x|)$ for $t<1$. The corresponding gradient calculation additionally uses the derivative bound and its norm convention. These estimates are absent from the linked definition.
pdf-item-equation-4-1.Breakdown.IsSimilarityProfile: Smooth $W,q$ satisfying the similarity equation and $\operatorname{div}W=0$ everywhere, with $\|D_y^jW\|\le C(1+|y|)^{-j-1}$ for $j=0,1,2$ and $|\nabla q|\le C(1+|y|)^{-3}$. The second-derivative and pressure bounds are extra compared with (1.2) and (1.3). The zero field is included. The paper's Frobenius gradient norm can be up to $\sqrt3$ times that operator norm.
pdf-item-equation-4-1.Breakdown.embeddedProfileOrbit_holds: `embeddedProfileOrbit_holds` uses spatial decay of a smooth recurrent similarity profile through two velocity derivatives and the pressure gradient. It reads the slices as a continuous nonzero homogeneous $H^1$ orbit with the same recurrence up to symmetry. The physical pointwise bounds in (4.1) come from applying the change of variables to the assumed decay.
pdf-item-equation-4-1.Breakdown.physicalMild_unconditional: The displayed bounds come from evaluating the spatial decay at $y=x/\sqrt{1-t}$. `physicalMild_unconditional` uses a smooth decaying profile and continuity of its slices in the homogeneous $H^1$ norm to prove that the resulting undilated velocity solves the mild equation on each $[0,T]$ with $T<1$.

ns-s4-006.Breakdown.Freq.gradSixDecay: For a smooth divergence-free $f:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ satisfying $|f(x)|\le C/(1+|x|)$ and $\|Df(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C/(1+|x|)^2$, the formal theorem proves $f\in L^6$ and a Sobolev bound by $(\int\sum_i|\partial_i f|^2)^{1/2}$. Its proof establishes integrability of the squared coordinate derivatives. The paper applies the same decay mechanism to $u^*(t)$ for each fixed $t<1$, with denominator $\sqrt{1-t}+|x|$. Identifying that physical slice with the theorem's input requires the profile-decay and positive-dilation facts. The linked theorem does not state membership of the two radial comparison functions themselves.

ns-s4-007.Breakdown.embeddedProfileOrbit_holds: `embeddedProfileOrbit_holds` turns the smooth, solenoidal, nonzero, decaying profile into a continuous curve of homogeneous $H^1$ states. Recurrence up to $R$ becomes recurrence up to the induced isometry on states. This is the similarity-coordinate input for the physical curve discussed in Proposition 4.1.
ns-s4-007.Breakdown.physicalMild_unconditional: `physicalMild_unconditional` gives the continuous mild curve obtained from (1.4) on each closed interval $[0,T]$ before the singular time $1$, for any similarity phase. It assumes a smooth decaying profile with continuous homogeneous $H^1$ slices. The mild-solution argument does not need the recurrence or nonzero conditions of Proposition 4.1.

pdf-item-equation-4-2.Breakdown.MildFramework.IsOrbit: Let $\rho$ be a surjective linear isometry of the real Hilbert space $X$. Let $S>0$ and let $w:\mathbb R\to X$ be continuous and nonzero somewhere, with $w(s+S)=\rho w(s)$. For $a\le s$, require the Bochner integral to exist and $w(s)=D_{e^{-(s-a)}}G(1-e^{-(s-a)})w(a)+\int_a^sD_{e^{-(s-r)}}K(1-e^{-(s-r)})(w(r),w(r))\,dr$. Here $G$, $K$ and $D$ are the heat, bilinear and dilation operators of the abstract setting, and the paper’s field is $u^*(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(-\log(1-t))$. The recurrence component of the formal condition is $w(s+S)=\rho_Rw(s)$ for all real $s$. For $\lambda=e^{-S}$, the paper's physical identity follows by the logarithmic change of time together with $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$ and commutation of $\rho_R$ with the dilations. That identity is not written in this condition.
pdf-item-equation-4-2.Breakdown.MildFramework.selfSimilar: For any curve $w:\mathbb R\to X$ in a real Hilbert space with dilation maps $D_\mu$, the formal function is $u_{s_0}(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(s_0-\log(1-t))$. On $t<1$ its scale is positive. The definition requires no recurrence, continuity or equation. In the paper $D_\mu f(x)=\sqrt\mu f(\sqrt\mu x)$. For $s_0=0$, $S>0$ and $\lambda=e^{-S}$, the paper's recurrence additionally needs $w(s+S)=\rho_Rw(s)$, commutation of $\rho_R$ with $D_\mu$ and the dilation composition law. The definition alone imposes none of those recurrence hypotheses.
pdf-item-equation-4-2.Breakdown.ProfilePieceStatement: For a recurrent similarity-time mild solution $w$ and positive natural $k$, the pieces $u_n$ on $[0,L]$, $L=1-e^{-S/k}$, are continuous mild solutions with $D_\mu u_n(L)=u_{n+1}(0)$, $u_{n+k}=\rho u_n$ and $\|u_n\|\le e^{S/(4k)}M$. No positive lower bound on $\|u^*(t)\|$ is given. The paper's formula instead holds on a whole period for every $0\le\sigma<1$: $u^*(1-\lambda^n+\lambda^n\sigma)=\rho_R^nD_{\lambda^{-n}}u^*(\sigma)$, $\lambda=e^{-S}$. The formal assertion states matching and a one-period shift for the short pieces, without that whole-period identity as a conclusion.
pdf-item-equation-4-2.Breakdown.orbitBound: The isometry in (4.2) preserves the norm of the similarity orbit. `orbitBound` uses this at the level of the orbit $w$: its norm is a continuous periodic scalar function, hence bounded uniformly in similarity time. Passing to physical velocity adds the norm factor from dilation.
pdf-item-equation-4-2.Breakdown.orbitNorm: `orbitNorm` proves a positive lower bound for a nonzero recurrent mild orbit. Small enough data give a bounded physical mild solution by small-data theory and uniqueness. Dilation back into similarity variables would then force the norm to decay, and (4.2)'s recurrence makes it return to its old value after each period.
pdf-item-equation-4-2.Breakdown.Freq.DilationAlgebra: On the frequency-side model of $X=\dot H^1_{\mathrm{div}}(\mathbb R^3)$ used in the formalization, $D_\mu$ acts by $f(\xi)\mapsto\mu^{-1/2}f(\mu^{-1/2}\xi)$, which corresponds to the paper's $D_\mu u(x)=\sqrt\mu\,u(\sqrt\mu x)$, and $G(t)$ multiplies by $e^{-4\pi^2t|\xi|^2}$. The formal statement asserts, for $\mu,\eta>0$, $\|D_\mu x\|_X=\mu^{1/4}\|x\|_X$, $D_1=I$, $D_\mu D_\eta=D_{\mu\eta}$, $D_\mu G(\mu t)=G(t)D_\mu$ for $t\ge0$, and that $D_\mu$ is given by this frequency formula. At $\mu=(1-t)^{-1}$, $t<1$, this gives the factor $(1-t)^{-1/4}$. For $u^*(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(-\log(1-t))$, the two-sided estimate (4.4) also needs positive lower and finite upper bounds for $\|w(s)\|$. Neither orbit bound is part of this formal assertion.

ns-s4-009.Breakdown.physicalPressure: `physicalPressure` defines $p(t,x)=(1-t)^{-1}q(s_0-\log(1-t),x/\sqrt{1-t})$ for $t<1$, the pressure accompanying (1.4) at final time one. It asserts no equation. Values for $t\ge1$ are conventions, not a continuation. The formal pressure formula with phase zero and $t<1$ is exactly $(1-t)^{-1}q(-\log(1-t),x/\sqrt{1-t})$.

ns-s4-010.Breakdown.PhysicalMomentum: `PhysicalMomentum` isolates the time derivative of the physical velocity obtained by rescaling a smooth similarity profile. It states the momentum equation before time one, with pressure rescaled by $(1-t)^{-1}$. The hypotheses include decay through two velocity derivatives and of the pressure gradient. Smoothness and zero divergence are separate conclusions in the argument.

ns-s4-011.Breakdown.sliceGradientContinuous_holds: `sliceGradientContinuous_holds` proves continuity of the similarity slices in the gradient norm. The derivative bound of order $(1+|y|)^{-2}$ gives a square-integrable majorant for dominated convergence. The paper applies this reasoning to the physical slices, where continuity also uses the dilation and change of time variable.

ns-s4-012.Breakdown.PhysicalWeak: `PhysicalWeak` is the pressure-free identity for the physical velocity of a smooth decaying similarity profile. Testing with a compactly supported solenoidal field kills the pressure term. Integration by parts then gives the negative gradient pairing and the negative advection pairing as the time derivative. Passing from this identity to the mild equation is a separate step.
ns-s4-012.Breakdown.physicalMild_unconditional: If the slices of the decaying smooth similarity profile $W$ are continuous in the homogeneous $H^1$ norm, then for every phase $s_0$ and $0<T<1$, $u(t,x)=(1-t)^{-1/2}W(s_0-\log(1-t),x/\sqrt{1-t})$ is continuous and mild on $[0,T]$. No recurrence or nonvanishing is assumed. The paper invokes Lemma 3.6 after integration by parts. The formal theorem additionally assumes the profile estimates displayed here.

ns-s4-013.Breakdown.physicalMild_unconditional: `physicalMild_unconditional` proves the Duhamel equation on each closed interval $[0,b]$ with $0<b<1$. It takes a smooth similarity profile with the stated decay and continuous homogeneous $H^1$ slices. Every time before the singular time lies in one such interval, which gives the half-open conclusion in the passage.

ns-s4-014.Breakdown.MildFramework.selfSimilar: For any curve $w:\mathbb R\to X$ in a real Hilbert space with dilation maps $D_\mu$, the formal function is $u_{s_0}(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(s_0-\log(1-t))$. On $t<1$ its scale is positive. The definition requires no recurrence, continuity or equation. In the physical realization $D_\mu f(x)=\sqrt\mu f(\sqrt\mu x)$. At phase zero this is the paper's physical scaling. To deduce $u^*(1-e^{-S}(1-t))=\rho_RD_{e^S}u^*(t)$ for $t<1$, one must also use $w(s+S)=\rho_Rw(s)$, the dilation composition law and commutation with $\rho_R$. No recurrence is asserted by this definition.

ns-s4-015.Breakdown.embeddedProfileOrbit_holds: A smooth, divergence-free, decaying solution $W$ of the similarity equation with $W(s+S,y)=RW(s,R^{-1}y)$, nonzero somewhere, gives a continuous nonzero homogeneous $H^1$ curve $w$ with $w(s+S)=\rho_Rw(s)$ solving the similarity-time mild equation. The extra decay estimates stay hypotheses. The paper additionally argues through the physical map $u^*(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(-\log(1-t))$: recurrence transports nonvanishing to nonnegative similarity time.

ns-s4-016.Breakdown.physicalTime: `physicalTime` defines $s=s_0-\log(1-t)$, which at $s_0=0$ is the similarity time $\log(1/(1-t))$ of (1.4) with $T=1$. Values for $t\ge1$ are conventions. The paper uses $\log(T/(T-t))$ for general $T$. For $t<1$ and $\lambda=e^{-S}$, the formal logarithmic change of variables increases by $S$ at the displayed time.

ns-s4-017.Breakdown.MildFramework.gluePieces: For $0<\mu<1$ and continuous curves $a_n:[0,1-\mu]\to X$ in a real Hilbert space with dilations $D_\mu$, the formal reconstruction is $v(t)=D_{\mu^{-n}}a_n(\sigma)$, $n=\lfloor\log(1-t)/\log\mu\rfloor_{\mathbb N}$ and $\sigma=(t-(1-\mu^n))/\mu^n$. On $0\le t<1$ this gives $0\le\sigma<1-\mu$ and $1-t=\mu^n(1-\sigma)$. The natural-number floor is zero on negative inputs. Outside each interval a curve is extended by its endpoint value. The formal construction generally takes $\mu=e^{-S/k}$, so one similarity period contains $k$ short intervals. The paper's times $t_n=1-\lambda^n$, $\lambda=e^{-S}$, are whole-period endpoints. They correspond to $k=1$, or to every kth short endpoint. Neither recurrence nor a norm rate is a conclusion of the reconstruction definition.

ns-s4-018.Breakdown.MildFramework.selfSimilar: For any curve $w:\mathbb R\to X$ in a real Hilbert space with dilation maps $D_\mu$, the formal function is $u_{s_0}(t)=D_{(1-t)^{-1}}w(s_0-\log(1-t))$. ns-s4-018.Breakdown.stepData: The identity in Lemma 4.2 lets successive intervals use dilated profile pieces. `stepData` uses the spectral dichotomy to add a finite-dimensional datum correction and a bounded right inverse for the resulting linear sequence equations. The profile identity is an input to that construction through `profilePiece`.
ns-s4-018.Breakdown.exists_section: Let $X$ be a real Banach space, $P:X\to X$ a bounded projection with finite-dimensional range, and $C\subset X$ a dense linear subspace. The theorem gives a bounded linear $J:X\to X$ with $PJ=P$ and $J(X)\subset C$. The restriction of $J$ to $\operatorname{ran}P$ is injective, so $E=J(\operatorname{ran}P)$ is finite-dimensional. Taking $C=C^\infty_{c,\mathrm{div}}$ inside $\dot H^1_{\mathrm{div}}$ supplies the correction space in the paper. The theorem supplies no inverse for the evolution equation or global weighted curve.

ns-s4-019.Breakdown.orbitBound: `orbitBound` supplies the upper constant before the physical dilation. For the exact background $a=u^*$ and prescribed perturbation datum $x=\chi+\gamma$, the Lean conclusion gives $v(0)=\chi+\gamma$. The paper also allows an arbitrary approximate background and a linear correction map $J:E\to X$. These are not part of this exact-background implication.

ns5.purpose.Breakdown.TransferHolds: The whole-space transfer in this section needs initial data with compact support. `TransferHolds` asserts that for any dense linear subspace and any positive tolerance one can select a datum in that subspace near the profile slice, with a mild curve converging to the profile in similarity coordinates. Symmetry of the second derivatives of $\chi$ then gives $\operatorname{div}(\nabla\chi\times A)=-\nabla\chi\cdot g$. This cancels the divergence introduced by $\chi g$ and proves the smooth cutoff is solenoidal.

The chosen parameter and force cancellation are hidden by its existential conclusion.

ns7-data-s039.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData: For natural $n$, certificate data are arbitrary real functions and fields: symmetries, period, approximate profile, weak Hessian, forcing and constraint fields, weight, adjoint fields and scalar bounds. No equations, signs, regularity or inequalities are imposed. Those are separate hypotheses. The scalar constants are parameter-independent data, while the period, fields, residual bounds and other named maps have their specified parameter arguments.

ns7-data-s040.Breakdown.weightedEnergy: `weightedEnergy` defines $\int_{[0,1]}\int(|\operatorname{tr}H|^2+w|G|_{\rm F}^2)$, equal to $\|v\|_w^2$ in (7.14) for $G=\nabla v$, $H=\nabla^2v$. Negative densities are truncated and an infinite integral is set to zero. For admissible perturbations and weights these conventions change nothing. The perturbation energy weights the squared gradient and includes the squared Laplacian.

ns7-data-s041.Breakdown.Cert.IsAdmissibleWeight: A weight $w$ is admissible when $w_*>0$, $w$ is measurable, $w\ge w_*$ everywhere and $w$ is bounded above. These are the assumptions in (7.14). Symmetry of $w$ is added separately in the full certificate. `IsAdmissibleWeight` gives exactly boundedness, measurability and the positive lower bound on the spatial weight.
ns7-data-s041.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.multipli: Certificate hypothesis: the weight $\omega$ on the Euclidean norm of the force coefficients is strictly positive, so $\|(v,\beta)\|_{w,\omega}^2=\|v\|_w^2+\omega^2|\beta|^2$ and divisions by $\omega$ are legitimate. No value of $\omega$ is fixed.
ns7-data-s041.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.weightFn: Certificate hypothesis: $w(Ry)=w(y)$ for every $(R,\theta_0)\in\Gamma$ and $y\in\mathbb R^3$. The paper's abstract certificate in Section 7.3 does not impose this symmetry. It is automatic for constant weights but extra for a general weight. The complete formal certificate additionally requires the spatial weight to be invariant under every prescribed orthogonal symmetry.

ns7-data-s042.Breakdown.weightedEnergy: `weightedEnergy` defines $\int_{[0,1]}\int(|\operatorname{tr}H|^2+w|G|_{\rm F}^2)$, equal to $\|v\|_w^2$ in (7.14) for $G=\nabla v$, $H=\nabla^2v$. Negative densities are truncated and an infinite integral is set to zero. For admissible perturbations and weights these conventions change nothing. `weightedEnergy` gives the period energy, with Frobenius gradient norm.
ns7-data-s042.Breakdown.stationaryEnergy: `stationaryEnergy` defines $\int_{\mathbb R^3}|\operatorname{tr}H|^2+\int_{\mathbb R^3}w|G|_{\rm F}^2$ for $G=\nabla u$, $H=\nabla^2u$. For $u\in\dot H^1_{\mathrm{div}}\cap L^6$ with $\Delta u\in L^2$ and a bounded positive measurable weight it equals $|u|_w^2$ in (7.14). There is no time integral. `stationaryEnergy` gives the instantaneous energy.
ns7-data-s042.Breakdown.Cert.sizeZ: `sizeZ` defines $(E_w(v)+\sum_i\beta_i^2)^{1/2}$, which for an admissible weight equals $\|(v,\beta)\|_{w,1}$. The coefficient weight is one. a general $\omega$ in (7.14) is handled by rescaling the forcing fields and coefficients first. This combined norm has coefficient weight one. The general positive weight is obtained by rescaling.
ns7-data-s042.Breakdown.supBoundFactor: `supBoundFactor` defines $c_w=1/\sqrt{2\pi(2\sqrt{w_*})}$, which for $w_*>0$ is $(4\pi\sqrt{w_*})^{-1/2}$ as in (7.15) and (7.48). For $w_*\le0$ the conventions $\sqrt{w_*}=0$ and $1/0=0$ give $c_w=0$, a range never used. For positive $w_*$ the scalar is exactly $(4\pi\sqrt{w_*})^{-1/2}$.

ns7-data-s043.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: `coercive` is the a priori estimate for the reference linearization, assumed uniformly over admissible perturbations.

ns7-data-s044.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.gap_tran: Assumed certificate inequality: for every weak period-one perturbation $v$, $\int_0^1\int|((W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}-W_\alpha^{\mathrm r})\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)(W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}-W_\alpha^{\mathrm r})|^2\le c_{\mathrm r}^2\|v\|_w^2$, the squared form of (7.19) when $c_{\mathrm r}\ge0$. `gap_transfer` bounds the change from reference to approximate convection by the same weighted perturbation norm.

ns7-data-s045.Breakdown.Cert.sliceConvection: `sliceConvection` defines $\sum_jW_j\partial_jv+(DW)v$ for solenoidal $v\in\dot H^1\cap L^6$, with $DW$ taken as zero where $W$ is not differentiable. For a differentiable profile it is exactly $(W\cdot\nabla)v+(v\cdot\nabla)W$, as in (7.13) and (7.16). Inserting the reference profile gives exactly the displayed reference convection formula.

ns7-data-s046.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: Assumed certificate inequality: for every weak period-one perturbation $v$ and $F\simeq\mathcal T_Sv+\mathcal C_\alpha^{\mathrm r}v+\sum_i\beta_ib_i$, $(\|v\|_w^2+\omega^2|\beta|^2)^{1/2}\le c_1\|F\|_{\mathcal H}+[F]+c_2|\ell(v)|$. The certificate requires $c_2\ge0$. The paper permits real $c_2$. The estimate measures the same right side in its full period norm and in a finite seminorm, with a separate constraint term.

ns7-data-s047.Breakdown.rowNorm: For arbitrary fields $F,e_k$ and real weights $\tau_k$, the formal definition is $[F]=(\sum_k\tau_k\langle F,e_k\rangle^2)^{1/2}$, using the iterated pairing over $[0,1]\times\mathbb R^3$. It imposes no orthogonality, sign, periodicity or integrability condition. The separate certificate conditions make $e_k$ orthonormal in $\mathcal H$ and require $0\le\tau_k\le c_0^2$. Replacing them by $\sqrt{\tau_k}e_k$ then gives the paper’s fields and seminorm. The definition itself gives no Bessel bound. This defines the weighted finite pairing expression. It does not prove its upper bound.
ns7-data-s047.Breakdown.Cert.rowNormHolds: For $c_0\ge0$, orthonormal period-one $e_k\in\mathcal H$, $0\le\tau_k\le c_0^2$ and $F,F′\in\mathcal H$, the seminorm $[F]$ satisfies $[F+F′]\le[F]+[F′]$, $[-F]=[F]$ and $[F]\le c_0\|F\|_{\mathcal H}$, as in (7.17).

ns7-data-s048.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: Certificate hypothesis: the coefficient $c_2$ of $|\ell(v)|$ in the a priori estimate satisfies $c_2\ge0$. Section 7.3 permits $c_2\in\mathbb R$, so this is an additional sign restriction. The formal certificate requires $c_2\ge0$, whereas the paper explicitly allows any real $c_2$.

ns7-data-s049.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: Assumed certificate inequality: for every weak period-one perturbation $v$ and $F\simeq\mathcal T_Sv+\mathcal C_\alpha^{\mathrm r}v+\sum_i\beta_ib_i$, $(\|v\|_w^2+\omega^2|\beta|^2)^{1/2}\le c_1\|F\|_{\mathcal H}+[F]+c_2|\ell(v)|$. The certificate requires $c_2\ge0$. The paper permits real $c_2$. For the stated weak-domain interpretation and finite weighted seminorm, the formal hypothesis has exactly the displayed norm, force, right-side and constraint terms.

ns7-data-s050.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: Assumed certificate inequality: for every weak period-one perturbation $v$ and $F\simeq\mathcal T_Sv+\mathcal C_\alpha^{\mathrm r}v+\sum_i\beta_ib_i$, $(\|v\|_w^2+\omega^2|\beta|^2)^{1/2}\le c_1\|F\|_{\mathcal H}+[F]+c_2|\ell(v)|$. ns7-data-s050.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.adjoint_: Assumed certificate inequality (7.33): for every weak perturbation $v$ and every period-one $F\simeq\mathcal T_Sv+\mathcal C_\alpha v$, $|\langle F,\psi_{\alpha,j}\rangle_{\mathcal H}-\sum_lY_{jl}(\alpha)\ell_l(v)|\le a_j\|v\|_w$, over every unprojected $F$ in the weak relation. ns7-data-s052.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.transf: `transferLoss` defines $\vartheta=(c_1+c_0)c_{\mathrm r}$ from the reference a priori coefficient, the seminorm bound and the convection-change bound. No sign or smallness is asserted. The certificate separately requires nonnegativity and $\vartheta<1$.

It is assumed, not derived from a size bound on the data. The transfer loss is strictly less than one. This field states the first of the two inequalities.
ns7-data-s052.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.coercive: Certificate hypothesis: $c_1+c_0\le(1-\vartheta)c_L$ with $\vartheta<1$ and $c_L>0$. The same inequality relates the absorbed coefficients to $c_L$. This field states the second of the two inequalities.

ns7-data-s053.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.atProf: With $\vartheta=(c_1+c_0)c_{\mathrm r}$, replaces $W^{\mathrm r}$ by $W^{\mathrm a}$, sets the gap and form shift to zero, divides $c_1,c_2,c_0$ and the residual seminorm bound by $1-\vartheta$ and the seminorm weights by $(1-\vartheta)^2$. A separate theorem shows the result is a certificate. This transformation makes reference and approximate profiles equal and the gap zero. Zero row count additionally makes the finite seminorm vanish.

ns7-data-s054.Breakdown.weightedEnergy: `weightedEnergy` defines $\int_{[0,1]}\int(|\operatorname{tr}H|^2+w|G|_{\rm F}^2)$, equal to $\|v\|_w^2$ in (7.14) for $G=\nabla v$, $H=\nabla^2v$. Negative densities are truncated and an infinite integral is set to zero. For admissible perturbations and weights these conventions change nothing. Since $w\ge w_*>0$, the energy controls the time average of the squared Frobenius gradient norm.

ns7-data-s055.Breakdown.Cert.Internal.ExtendedFrozenBr: From the reference form bound, the form-shift bound and $c_{3,\mathrm r}+c_{3,\mathrm{shift}}\le c_3$, the frozen form at $W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}(\theta)$ is at least $-c_3\int(|\Delta u|^2+w|\nabla u|^2)$ for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$, every real $\theta$ and every invariant solenoidal $u$. `profile_form` gives (7.22) for every real time and every spatially invariant admissible field, using the reference bound and its transfer allowance.

ns7-data-s056.Breakdown.Cert.ExtendedSupBoundHolds: `ExtendedSupBoundHolds` specifies, for the constructed $v=\mathcal T_S^{-1}f$, that $U=\operatorname*{ess\,sup}_\theta\|\nabla v(\theta)\|_2$ is finite and $U^2\le[w_*^{-1}+2Sc_3/m]\|v\|_w^2+(2S/m)(\|F\|_{\mathcal H}+b_*|\beta|)\|v\|_w$, with $m=2$ only under a half-period symmetry. The formal proposition specifies the resulting supremum estimate for inverse solutions, with the same period factor. It does not itself state the differentiated energy identity.

ns7-data-s057.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.IsHeld: A supplied $f\in\mathcal H_{\rm div}^\Gamma$, $\beta$ is a bounded correction when, with $v=\mathcal T_S^{-1}f$, the projected equation holds, $\ell(v)=\bar\ell(\alpha)$, $(E_w(v)+|\beta|^2)^{1/2}\le2\varepsilon$ and $U(v)\le M$. Weight one: $\omega\beta$, $b_i/\omega$ replace $\beta,b_i$. The two bounds are part of this formal condition, but its coefficient norm is normalized to weight one and its time bound is an essential supremum.

ns7-data-s058.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData: For natural $n$, certificate data are arbitrary real functions and fields: symmetries, period, approximate profile, weak Hessian, forcing and constraint fields, weight, adjoint fields and scalar bounds. No equations, signs, regularity or inequalities are imposed. Those are separate hypotheses. The residual norm and seminorm bounds are arbitrary real functions of the parameter, and their uniform upper bound is a real constant.

With $\delta\ge0$ this is $\|F_\alpha^{\mathrm a}\|_{\mathcal H}\le\delta(\alpha)$. It bounds the residual including its gradient part, before Leray projection. ns7-data-s059.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.defect_l: Certificate hypothesis: $\delta(\alpha)\le\delta_{\max}$ for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$. With $\|F_\alpha^{\mathrm a}\|_{\mathcal H}\le\delta(\alpha)$ this is a uniform bound on the full residual. Continuity of $\delta$ or of the residual is not included.

ns7-data-s060.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.small_fi: Certificate hypothesis: $2c_Lc_wM<1$ with $c_w=(4\pi\sqrt{w_*})^{-1/2}$, exactly (7.25). In the formal construction it bounds the contraction factor of the nonlinear map at a fixed parameter. The strict first smallness condition agrees.

It does not build the paper's joint map on $\mathcal K\times\mathcal Z$ and uses (7.26), which the paper says is unused. The paper says its later argument does not use (7.26). ns7-data-s062.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.nontrivi: Certificate hypothesis: $4\varepsilon^2/w_*<\int_0^1\int|\nabla W_\alpha^{\mathrm a}|^2$ for every $\alpha\in\mathcal K$. Multiplying by $w_*$ gives (7.28). An infinite integral is converted to zero, so the strict inequality excludes it. The formal strict inequality is the displayed condition divided by positive $w_*$.
ns7-data-s062.Breakdown.Cert.extendedHeldNonzeroHolds_: If $w\ge w_*>0$, $(E_w(v)+|\beta|^2)^{1/2}\le2\varepsilon$ and $4\varepsilon^2/w_*<\int_0^1\int|\nabla W_\alpha^{\rm a}|_F^2$, then $W_\alpha^{\rm a}+v$ is not zero almost everywhere in space-time. It does not assert that the zero set has measure zero. `extendedHeldNonzeroHolds_of` derives nonvanishing from that strict inequality and the bounded perturbation. It is a consequence of the condition.

ns7-data-s063.Breakdown.ExtendedCertificateData.params: `params` defines $\mathcal K=\{\alpha:|\alpha_j|\le\varrho_j\ (j\in\mathcal J),\ \sum_{j\notin\mathcal J}(d_j\alpha_j)^2\le\varrho_*^2\}$, exactly (7.29). Under nonnegative radii and nonzero scales it is nonempty, compact and convex, possibly with empty interior. `params` uses exactly a selected coordinate subset, interval radii and a complementary scaled ball.
ns7-data-s063.Breakdown.IsExtendedCertificate.scale_ne: Certificate hypothesis: every scale $d_j$ is nonzero, so the update $\alpha_j-d_j^{-1}V_j\cdot\Phi(\alpha)$ uses the ordinary reciprocal. No common sign is required, and the condition is empty when there are no coordinates.

ns7-data-s069.Breakdown.Cert.ExtendedAdjointEnclosureH: `ExtendedAdjointEnclosureHolds` specifies, for normalized certificates and a bounded nonlinear correction, $|V_j\cdot\beta+\langle F_\alpha^{\mathrm a},\psi_{\alpha,j}\rangle+(Y\bar\ell)_j|\le\widetilde a_j(2\varepsilon)^2+2\varepsilon\sqrt{a_j^2+|\langle b,\psi_{\alpha,j}\rangle-V_j|^2/\omega^2}$ for each $j\in\mathcal J$. `ExtendedAdjointEnclosureHolds` supplies the separate-coordinate enclosure after pairing the equation and using the combined bound.
